abstract: Maintains flood plain elevation, storm surge clearance, and subterranean water table ingress records
system_message:
You are the Geotechnical flood hydrologist (HYDRO), responsible for maintaining flood plain elevation, storm surge clearance, and subterranean water table ingress records, as well as tracking soil drainage permeability assessments across candidate cultural heritage evacuation facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Soil drainage permeability（SOIL）
information_points.content:
HYDRO-SOIL-P1H：For Valley Ridge Reinforced Bunkered Archive, the surrounding soil permeability rate across the upper soil strata surrounding the vault foundation is 30 mm/h, based on the runoff water infiltration rate from the geotechnical percolation survey.
HYDRO-SOIL-9IA：The geotechnical percolation survey for Pine Crest Decommissioned Military Bunker documents a surrounding soil permeability rate of 10 mm/h through the native soil strata surrounding the vault foundation.
HYDRO-SOIL-QTE：Geotechnical percolation survey measurements show that the surrounding soil permeability rate in the upper soil strata surrounding the foundation of Highland Granite Subterranean Repository is 20 mm/h.

information_points.title: Maintains flood plain elevation, storm surge clearance, and subterranean water table ingress records（ELEV）
information_points.content:
HYDRO-ELEV-A8T：According to the hydrological flood risk assessment for Highland Granite Subterranean Repository, the primary intake threshold relative to the 100-year storm surge datum reflects a base elevation above peak storm surge of 9 m, measured as the vertical elevation difference between the lowest portal opening and the projected peak surge level.
HYDRO-ELEV-VSF：For Valley Ridge Reinforced Bunkered Archive, the hydrological flood risk assessment establishes that the base elevation above peak storm surge at the primary intake threshold relative to the 100-year storm surge datum is 3 m, measured as the vertical difference between the lowest portal opening and the projected peak surge level.
HYDRO-ELEV-XQF：The hydrological flood risk assessment records indicate that Pine Crest Decommissioned Military Bunker features a base elevation above peak storm surge of 9 m at its primary intake threshold relative to the 100-year storm surge datum, determined by the vertical elevation difference from the lowest portal opening to the projected peak surge level.
